findings.issue_text: [Medium/bug] integration.py (OAuthLoginView.dispatch) — safe_urlopen(url=..., data=data) is called outside the try/except; a non-200 response or network error will raise an unhandled exception and produce a 500 instead of the friendly error() page.

[Medium/bug] integration.py (GitHubInstallation.dispatch) — integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] can raise KeyError for pre-existing integrations whose metadata lacks a sender field, crashing the install flow instead of showing the error page.

[Medium/bug] integration.py (OAuthLoginView.dispatch) — request.GET.get("code") may be None (e.g. user denies authorize and GitHub redirects back with error= instead of code), which is passed into the token-exchange payload; also redirect_uri and state are interpolated into the authorize URL without urlencode(), which is fragile if values contain reserved characters.

[Low/bug] integration.py (GitHubInstallation.dispatch) — request.GET.get("installation_id", pipeline.fetch_state("installation_id")) treats an empty string (?installation_id=) as valid; only None is filtered, so an empty id falls through to Integration.DoesNotExist → pipeline.next_step() with an empty installation_id bound.

[Low/bug] integration.py (OAuthLoginView.dispatch) — installation_id is read and bound from request.GET before the state parameter is validated, so an unauthenticated callback request can write an attacker-chosen installation_id into the pipeline state; the bind should occur only after the state check.

[Medium/test_gap] test_integration.py — tests hardcode the pipeline state (9cae5e..., ddd023d...); the same hardcoded state string is reused across different pipelines (org_1 and org_2) in test_github_installed_on_another_org, masking the per-pipeline state binding the new code depends on; tests should extract the state from the actual redirect Location.

[Medium/test_gap] test_integration.py — no coverage for OAuth token-exchange failure paths (missing access_token, safe_urlread raising, GitHub returning an error param instead of code, user-info missing login), and no test that the sender-mismatch check is skipped/handled for legacy integrations without metadata["sender"].

[Low/doc_defect] pipeline_advancer.py — the change from FORWARD_INSTALL_FOR list to == "github" silently drops extensibility other providers might have relied on; worth a comment noting github-only behavior is intentional.

[Low/security] integration.py (error()/get_document_origin) — error_short is passed through _() in error() while defaults are already lazy translations; if a caller passes an already-translated string it will be double-looked-up, so the wrapping in error() should be removed.

[Low/bug] integration.py (OAuthLoginView.dispatch) — there is no csrf/method check beyond pipeline state that this is the same browser session; if pipeline.signature is predictable or logged, the OAuth code exchange could be replayed — verify pipeline.signature is a high-entropy per-session value (test constants like 9cae5e... suggest it may be a deterministic hash).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] integration.py (OAuthLoginView.dispatch) — safe_urlopen(url=..., data=data) is called outside the try/except; a non-200 response or network error will raise an unhandled exception and produce a 500 instead of the friendly error() page.

adjudication.rationale: In OAuthLoginView.dispatch, the token exchange does `req = safe_urlopen(url=..., data=data)` before the try/except that only wraps `safe_urlread(req).decode(...)` and `parse_qsl`. If `safe_urlopen` raises (e.g., network/HTTP error), it will bypass the friendly `error(...)` response and bubble up as a 500 since there’s no surrounding exception handling in this method.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] integration.py (GitHubInstallation.dispatch) — integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] can raise KeyError for pre-existing integrations whose metadata lacks a sender field, crashing the install flow instead of showing the error page.

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same bug: the code directly indexes integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] without ensuring the "sender" key exists, leading to a KeyError for integrations whose metadata lacks sender information (e.g., pre-existing/not set at creation).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] integration.py (OAuthLoginView.dispatch) — request.GET.get("code") may be None (e.g. user denies authorize and GitHub redirects back with error= instead of code), which is passed into the token-exchange payload; also redirect_uri and state are interpolated into the authorize URL without urlencode(), which is fragile if values contain reserved characters.

adjudication.rationale: In OAuthLoginView.dispatch, the authorize redirect URL is built via f"...authorize...?client_id=...&state={state}&redirect_uri={redirect_uri}" without URL-encoding query params (diff shows direct string interpolation), which is fragile if redirect_uri/state ever contain reserved characters. Also, the token-exchange payload sets "code": request.GET.get("code") with no explicit check for missing code (e.g. GitHub may return error=...); while the code later handles missing access_token by returning error(), the diff doesn’t show whether safe_urlopen can accept None for the payload, so this is a concrete robustness/edge-case concern rather than a provable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] integration.py (GitHubInstallation.dispatch) — request.GET.get("installation_id", pipeline.fetch_state("installation_id")) treats an empty string (?installation_id=) as valid; only None is filtered, so an empty id falls through to Integration.DoesNotExist → pipeline.next_step() with an empty installation_id bound.

adjudication.rationale: In `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`, `installation_id = request.GET.get("installation_id", pipeline.fetch_state("installation_id"))` will return an empty string when the query contains `?installation_id=`. The subsequent guard only checks `is None`, so `""` is treated as a valid id and is immediately persisted via `pipeline.bind_state("installation_id", installation_id)`. With `installation_id == ""`, the `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` lookup will raise `Integration.DoesNotExist`, hit the `except`, and `pipeline.next_step()` is called with the empty installation id bound. Additionally, because `request.GET.get` prefers the provided (empty) param over the pipeline state, an empty query param can override a valid `pipeline.fetch_state("installation_id")`, which is a behavior introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] integration.py (OAuthLoginView.dispatch) — installation_id is read and bound from request.GET before the state parameter is validated, so an unauthenticated callback request can write an attacker-chosen installation_id into the pipeline state; the bind should occur only after the state check.

adjudication.rationale: In OAuthLoginView.dispatch, `installation_id = request.GET.get("installation_id")` is immediately persisted via `pipeline.bind_state("installation_id", installation_id)` before any validation of the OAuth `state` parameter. The subsequent state check (`if request.GET.get("state") != pipeline.signature: return error(...)`) happens after the bind, so a request with a missing/invalid `state` can still mutate the pipeline state with an attacker-controlled `installation_id`. Later, GitHubInstallation reads `installation_id` from `pipeline.fetch_state("installation_id")`, so this mutation can affect the rest of the flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] test_integration.py — tests hardcode the pipeline state (9cae5e..., ddd023d...); the same hardcoded state string is reused across different pipelines (org_1 and org_2) in test_github_installed_on_another_org, masking the per-pipeline state binding the new code depends on; tests should extract the state from the actual redirect Location.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds OAuthLoginView which enforces `request.GET.get("state") == pipeline.signature` before exchanging the OAuth code. In tests, the OAuth `state` is hardcoded (e.g. `9cae5e...`, `ddd023d...`) and reused when hitting the setup callback (`setup_path_2` in `test_github_installed_on_another_org`, and other tests), rather than extracting it from the actual redirect Location produced by the init/setup flow. This makes tests brittle and can fail to validate the per-pipeline signature binding that the new code depends on.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] test_integration.py — no coverage for OAuth token-exchange failure paths (missing access_token, safe_urlread raising, GitHub returning an error param instead of code, user-info missing login), and no test that the sender-mismatch check is skipped/handled for legacy integrations without metadata["sender"].

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new nontrivial OAuth logic in `OAuthLoginView.dispatch` (token exchange via `safe_urlopen`/`safe_urlread`, parsing `parse_qsl`, then `get_user_info` and requiring `login`), but the added tests only cover the happy path and the sender-login mismatch case; they do not exercise failure branches like missing `access_token`, exceptions in `safe_urlread`/parsing, missing/invalid `code`/error responses, or `get_user_info` not returning `login`. Additionally, the new sender check in `GitHubInstallation.dispatch` directly indexes `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` without a guard, and there is no test covering behavior when that metadata is absent (as could be the case for older/legacy integrations).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc_defect] pipeline_advancer.py — the change from FORWARD_INSTALL_FOR list to == "github" silently drops extensibility other providers might have relied on; worth a comment noting github-only behavior is intentional.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the conditional from `provider_id in FORWARD_INSTALL_FOR` (where the list contained only `"github"`) to an explicit `provider_id == "github"`. This does not drop support for any existing provider, since no other providers were listed. Also, the diff already includes an explicit comment immediately above the check explaining this github-only forwarding behavior, so the request for an additional comment is not grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/security] integration.py (error()/get_document_origin) — error_short is passed through _() in error() while defaults are already lazy translations; if a caller passes an already-translated string it will be double-looked-up, so the wrapping in error() should be removed.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, only `error_short` is wrapped in `_()` inside `error()` (`{"error": _(error_short)}`), but the default `error_short` is a plain string (`"Invalid installation request."`), not a lazy-translated value. The lazy-translated default is `error_long` (`ERR_INTEGRATION_INVALID_INSTALLATION_REQUEST`), which is not wrapped again. Call sites shown pass plain string literals for `error_short`, so the claimed “defaults are already lazy translations” / “double-looked-up” issue is not verifiable from this diff and reads as a theoretical/style concern rather than an actual defect introduced here.
